svg.aria-label: Diagram of the MedSSL pipeline: the COVID-19 Radiography Database is split into a fixed held-out test set and an unlabeled dev pool; a ResNet-50 encoder is self-supervised pretrained with SimCLR on the dev pool to produce a single checkpoint; that checkpoint is then reused, reloaded fresh from disk, in three tracks -- a label-efficiency grid of linear-probe and from-scratch baselines, a semi-supervised pseudo-labeling fine-tune at 1 percent labels, and unsupervised k-means and GMM clustering with post-hoc validation -- and every track is scored on the same held-out test split.
svg.title: MedSSL Method Overview
svg.desc: The COVID-19 Radiography Database (21,165 images, 4 classes) is split, seeded, into a fixed held-out test set (labels kept, reused by every track) and an unlabeled dev pool. A ResNet-50 encoder is self-supervised pretrained on the dev pool with SimCLR (NT-Xent loss), producing a single pretrained checkpoint. That checkpoint is the shared starting point for three tracks, each reloading it fresh from disk: (2a) a label-efficiency grid comparing SSL, ImageNet-pretrained, and from-scratch conditions at 1/10/100% labels, producing the label-efficiency curve; (2b) semi-supervised fine-tuning via confidence-thresholded pseudo-labeling at 1% labels, compared against the same-fraction baselines; (2c) frozen-embedding k-means/GMM clustering and anomaly detection, validated post-hoc against true labels, visualized as a cluster-vs-true-label UMAP scatter. Every outcome is scored on the same seeded, held-out test split.
svg.text: One shared ResNet-50 encoder, three learning paradigms (self-supervised · semi-supervised · unsupervised)
